page: Microsoft Azure F8-2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture operating at 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 32.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 945 GB, and the instance is premium storage capable. No GPUs are present on this server type.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance alongside moderate multi-core capabilities. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and Geekbench single-core score both rank in the top tier (top 10%), supported by top-tier single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, due to the low core count of 2 vCPUs, multi-threaded and multi-core benchmarks such as the Passmark CPU score, Geekbench software compilation, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the weak category (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 6.72 million operations per second, consistently register in the average range (middle 50%).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F8-2amds_v7 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The combination of 64.0 GB of RAM, 945 GB of local storage, and strong single-thread performance makes this server type suitable for database operations, caching layers, text processing, and lightweight memory-intensive applications. Conversely, it is less suitable for highly parallelized tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or large-scale language model inference, where its low core count and poor medium-model prompt processing speeds present clear performance tradeoffs.
